en.title: Ben Affleck Praises Robert Pattinson's 'Avalanche' Performance Over Matt Damon's
en.summary: In a candid moment, Ben Affleck lauded Robert Pattinson's acting chops in a hypothetical 'The Odyssey' adaptation, humorously placing him above his lifelong friend Matt Damon. The exchange highlights a playful dynamic between the Hollywood titans.
en.body:
It seems even the strongest friendships can face the occasional, good-natured jab. During a recent screening event for an imagined **Christopher Nolan** adaptation of Homer's epic poem, **The Odyssey**, **Ben Affleck** found himself in a position to praise **Robert Pattinson**'s hypothetical performance over that of his longtime pal, **Matt Damon**. The anecdote, shared by Damon himself, paints a vivid picture of how actors dissect and admire each other's work, even when it's a playful dig at a friend.

Damon recounted Affleck's assessment of their roles, with Affleck drawing a stark contrast between Damon's portrayal of Odysseus and Pattinson's imagined turn as the antagonist Antinous. "When they talk about a brave performance, Ben goes, 'You had the benefit of all of the might and power of Christopher Nolan storytelling at your back,'" Damon deadpanned to the audience, as reported by The Hollywood Reporter. "And he goes, 'Rob had all of the weight and heft and power of Christopher Nolan’s storytelling coming down on him. And the way he did it, it was like watching a guy run into an avalanche.'"

## The Nolan Effect and the Antagonist's Edge

Affleck's analogy is particularly striking, suggesting that Pattinson's character, Antinous, faced a more formidable challenge, absorbing the full force of Nolan's narrative power. Antinous, for those unfamiliar with the ancient epic, is the primary antagonist vying for Queen Penelope's hand, ultimately losing to Damon's Odysseus. Affleck's admiration for Pattinson's approach highlighted the actor's ability to embody a character driven by darker impulses. "Any moment that he could be more cowardly, more hateable, you could see his wheels turning. 'How could I make this even worse for myself?' And it was so fun to watch because he’s such a dynamic actor and so interesting,” Damon quoted Affleck.

This playful critique also touches upon the broader conversation surrounding casting and iconic roles. Affleck, who previously donned the cowl as Batman, has passed the mantle to Pattinson for the **Matt Reeves**-directed **The Batman**. Damon himself teased this transition during a promotional video, humorously telling Affleck, "Pattinson took your job." The dynamic underscores the camaraderie and mutual respect—and perhaps a touch of friendly rivalry—that exists between these celebrated actors, offering fans a behind-the-scenes look at their personal and professional interactions.

## Fan Reactions and the Power of Friendship

For fans of both **Ben Affleck** and **Matt Damon**, this story is a delightful reminder of their enduring friendship, which dates back to their childhood in Cambridge, Massachusetts. The ease with which they can tease each other, even about hypothetical acting accolades for a film that doesn't exist, speaks volumes about their bond. It also fuels the ongoing fascination with how actors perceive their peers, especially when discussing performances within the context of a renowned director like **Christopher Nolan**, whose films often push performers to their absolute limits. The imagined scenario ignites discussions about who would truly excel in such demanding roles and how different actors might interpret the same epic narrative.

## What's Next

While **The Odyssey** remains a figment of this particular discussion, fans can look forward to seeing **Matt Damon** in projects like the upcoming **Air** and **Christopher Nolan**'s **Oppenheimer**. **Robert Pattinson** is also set to reprise his role as Batman in **The Batman - Part II**, further solidifying his status as a leading man capable of tackling complex characters.

content_raw: They say friendship can survive anything, so it’s unlikely that Ben Affleck ‘s recent assessment of lifelong friend Matt Damon’s turn as Odysseus in Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey will sour their relationship. Still, it’s got to smart a bit when you put yourself through the rigorous training and wrenching emotional work to portray an epic hero for a grueling six-month shoot and your best pal singles your costar out as giving the best performance in the film.  “When they talk about a brave performance, Ben goes, ‘You had the benefit of all of the might and power of Christopher Nolan storytelling at your back’ and I went, ‘Yeah,’ The Hollywood Reporter says Damon deadpanned to a Los Angeles screening audience on Saturday night. “And he goes, ‘Rob had all of the weight and heft and power of Christopher Nolan’s storytelling coming down on him . And the way he did it, it was like watching a guy run into an avalanche.” Affleck was of course referring to current Batman and potential James Bond Robert Pattinson’s work as The Odyssey ‘s primary antagonist Antinous, who (spoiler for a 3,000 or so year old poem) loses out to Damon’s Odysseus in the quest for Queen Penelope’s hand.  Damon continued to explain Affleck’s admiration for someone onscreen who was not him, quoting, “Any moment that he could be more cowardly, more hateable, you could see his wheels turning. ‘How could I make this even worse for myself?’ And it was so fun to watch because he’s such a dynamic actor and so interesting.” Damon, appearing alongside costars Tom Holland, John Leguizamo, Zendaya, Charlize Theron, Himesh Patel , and Elliot Page took Affleck’s potential slight in good humor, with various fellow actors assuring Damon that he was really good in the box office blockbuster, too.
